name: Savannah River Site
notes: Reactor-neutrino physics happened here only as a guest experiment: the site is a DOE production and cleanup site, not a physics laboratory.

The official SRS timeline lists "Neutrino confirmed at P Reactor" under 1956 and "R Reactor startup" under an earlier year heading whose digits were lost in the page text; the active interval therefore starts with the 1954 P, L, K reactor startups and is marked approximate.

summary.plain: A very large U.S. Department of Energy site in South Carolina, built in the early 1950s to make nuclear-weapons materials. Its P Reactor gave Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines the intense stream of antineutrinos with which they detected the neutrino in 1956.
summary.technical: Savannah River Site (formerly Savannah River Plant): 310 square miles in Aiken, Barnwell and Allendale counties, South Carolina; five production reactors built from 1951 (R, P, K, L, C). Host of the Cowan–Reines reactor-antineutrino experiment at P Reactor, 1955-1956.
